# openssh / kex_fuzz

openssh's own fuzz target `kex_fuzz` ([source](source/kex_fuzz.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over openssh-portable (openssh/openssh-portable at 0ef0f5a8).

Runs full client/server key exchanges (5 KEX methods x RSA/ECDSA/Ed25519 host keys) with the input substituted for the server-to-client and then the client-to-server stream; every return code is only logged via debug_fr/error_fr.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against openssh-portable at commit 0ef0f5a8.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing, so a statement about it says only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer.

## Statements ([Statements.v](Statements.v), [Characterise.v](Characterise.v), [Distribution.v](Distribution.v))

**Some statements are blocked by the model.** On the inputs they cover, the binary opens files other than its input, which this release's model does not decode, so the statements marked "blocked by the model" are false in this model for that reason alone. The program is not at fault.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch openssh` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `kex_fuzz.plain` | 3,110,056 | `bdae6312a3cf6fd30384c470df8bbb33f28b36a6b2ef27217a7100146318f2a9` |
| ubsan | `kex_fuzz.ubsan` | 3,080,456 | `7b3590109f2d6ae638c6403e3505016824e8b30e74add35cc1dd3ffb94507356` |
| asan | `kex_fuzz.asan` | 4,408,744 | `8fa81b40b4ccc3ba89a1fc96c1df29c7982ea47555a222342bc810cf7135600e` |
| asan-ubsan | `kex_fuzz.asan-ubsan` | 4,191,048 | `862228d83813078173e40642b175352e47a4e9ffc03169d682c7e533dd965415` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libcrypto.a` (a library from the build image), `libz.a` (a library from the build image)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libcrypto.a` (a library from the build image), `libz.a` (a library from the build image)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libcrypto.a` (a library from the build image), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime), `libz.a` (a library from the build image)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libcrypto.a` (a library from the build image), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime), `libz.a` (a library from the build image)
